input_signals.name: SolvencyCoveredBookToMarket
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RANK(RATIO(oancf, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market is a mispricing signal when internal cash generation comfortably services the liability stack, and a distress signal when it does not; the balance-sheet quality dimension is solvency, not profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: Industry-ranking book-to-market removes sector-level accounting composition so the valuation channel reflects within-industry cheapness, while cash flow to total liabilities measures the firm's capacity to avoid a debt-driven equity wipeout. The interaction rewards cheap firms whose leverage is well covered and penalizes cheap, cash-poor, heavily obligated firms that populate the value-trap region of the book-to-market distribution.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( ratio( oancf, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitToEnterpriseValue
input_signals.expression: RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), SUB(ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)), che))
input_signals.hypothesis: The cleanest measure of quality value is the price paid for the most persistent, least manipulable profit line: gross profit capitalized against the whole claim structure net of cash, so that leverage and cash hoards cannot make a distressed firm look cheap.
input_signals.reasoning: Using enterprise value in the denominator means a cheap-looking equity that is cheap only because of heavy debt is automatically penalized, which is exactly the trap the story targets, while netting cash prevents cash-rich quality firms from being scored as expensive. Gross profit (revt minus cogs) is the quality-exclusive numerator with near-universal coverage, repairing the 0.09 coverage problem created by the operating-cash-flow leg. As a single ratio it also avoids the unstable rank-product portfolio composition of the gen-0 entries.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), sub( add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ), che ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, a multi-year improvement in gross profitability distinguishes mispriced turnarounds from melting-ice-cube traps whose low multiple correctly extrapolates fundamental decay.
input_signals.reasoning: The valuation leg is a depreciation-added cash earnings yield, which uses `dp` (quality-exclusive) to strip away non-cash charges without depending on the sparse cash-flow statement. The quality leg is the direction, not the level, of gross profitability, so the signal is not a restatement of RMW-style profitability sorts and can carry FF5 alpha. The rank product only rewards firms that are cheap and improving simultaneously.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( ib, dp ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.hypothesis: A high book-to-market is mispricing when the book equity was built from a cumulative history of retained profits and is a distress discount when the balance sheet is funded by liabilities against accumulated deficits.
input_signals.reasoning: Retained earnings relative to total liabilities is a stock (not flow) measure of cumulative earnings quality and solvency, so it separates mature self-funded value firms from levered loss-makers whose book equity is fragile. This tests whether the trap dimension is better captured by cumulative history than by contemporaneous cash conversion, which failed in gen 0. Coverage should be high since `re`, `lt`, `ceq`, and price are broadly reported.

input_signals.reasoning: Net working capital scaled by total liabilities is a Graham-style survival test built entirely from quality-exclusive items (`act`, `lct`, `lt`), giving a liquidity-based rather than profitability-based definition of quality, so it is not a repackaging of RMW. Pairing it with a cash earnings yield tests whether the trap mechanism is about short-run solvency timing rather than accounting aggressiveness. This makes the batch informative: profitability level (1), profitability dynamics (2), cumulative history (3), leverage interaction (4), deficit traps (5), and liquidity buffers (6) would each teach a different lesson.

input_signals.hypothesis: Trap separation is a conjunctive condition rather than a trade-off: a firm qualifies as quality value only if it is simultaneously cheap and resilient, so the score should be the weaker of the two ranks and no amount of cheapness should compensate for fragility.
input_signals.reasoning: Product and sum both allow one extreme leg to dominate, which is why they performed almost identically; MIN enforces a strict conjunction so the long decile contains only firms strong on both dimensions and the short decile contains firms failing at least one. This is the one structural variant that could actually change portfolio composition materially, making it a genuine test of the conditional story rather than an algebraic restatement.
